source_safety_review.claim: The required GitHub-prospect CSV writer preserves untrusted spreadsheet formula prefixes. Opening an exported CSV in software that interprets formula cells may evaluate those cells. This is a static source finding, not a claim that every CSV viewer evaluates formulas.

evidence.why: escape() only flattens newlines and quotes CSV delimiters; no prefix neutralization occurs before user-controlled profile columns are joined.

evidence.excerpt:
For dev-tool SaaS, GitHub is one of the highest-quality discovery channels:

1. Identify 3–5 "anchor" repos: your direct competitors, your category leader, complementary tools your buyer uses
2. Pull stargazers (or forks for stronger intent) via `node tools/clis/github-prospects.js stargazers <owner/repo> --enrich --with-company --format csv`
3. Filter to users with `company` set — these are the easiest to enrich downstream
4. Pair with Apollo/Clay/Hunter to lookup email by name + company
5. Validate with Truelist before adding to outreach list
evidence.why: The selected workflow explicitly invokes this helper with --enrich --with-company --format csv, so it is an actual authored dependency.

static_innocuous_example.method: Manually derived from the literal source branch; no upstream CLI/function or spreadsheet was executed.
static_innocuous_example.derivation: The company value has no newline, comma or double quote, so escape() returns =1+1 unchanged. The third CSV field therefore begins with =. Formula interpretation depends on the receiving spreadsheet/import mode.
